# Execution and output

The `[params]` section controls code execution, output settings, time-stepping,
and termination criteria. These parameters govern how the simulation runs, not
what it simulates.

See also: [Coupling loop](../../Explanations/coupling_loop.md) for how
time-stepping and convergence work in practice.

Every config file declares the schema version it is written against.

## Time-stepping `[params.dt]`

PROTEUS supports three time-stepping methods. The adaptive method is
recommended for production runs; proportional is useful for steady-state
problems; maximum gives a fixed step. The `atol`/`rtol`/`scale_*`/`window`
parameters apply to the adaptive method, `propconst` to the proportional
method, and the `mushy_*`/`hysteresis_*` parameters cap the step during the
solidification transition (melt fraction between `phi_crit` and
`mushy_upper`) so the rapid phase change stays resolved.

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED: config-table [params.dt] -->
<!-- Generated by tools/generate_config_reference.py; edit src/proteus/config/, not this table -->
| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `starspec` | float | `100000000.0` | Maximum interval at which to recalculate the stellar spectrum \[yr\]. Must be >= 0. |
| `starinst` | float | `100.0` | Maximum interval at which to recalculate instellation flux \[yr\]. Must be >= 0. |
| `method` | str | `"adaptive"` | Time-stepping method. Choices: `"proportional"`, `"adaptive"`, `"maximum"`. |
| `propconst` | float | `52.0` | Proportionality constant (proportional method). Must be > 0. |
| `atol` | float | `0.02` | Absolute tolerance on time-step size (adaptive method) \[yr\]. Must be > 0. |
| `rtol` | float | `0.1` | Relative tolerance on time-step size (adaptive method) \[dimensionless\]. Must be > 0. |
| `scale_incr` | float | `1.6` | Scale factor to grow time-step on a successful adaptive step \[dimensionless, must be >1\]. Must be > 1. |
| `scale_decr` | float | `0.8` | Scale factor to shrink time-step on a rejected adaptive step \[dimensionless, in (0, 1)\]. Must be > 0 and < 1. |
| `window` | int | `3` | Number of previous steps to consider for adaptive-method comparison \[dimensionless\]. Must be >= 1. |
| `minimum` | float | `100.0` | Minimum absolute time-step size \[yr\]. Must be > 0. |
| `minimum_rel` | float | `1e-05` | Minimum relative time-step size \[dimensionless\]. Must be > 0. |
| `maximum` | float | `10000000.0` | Maximum time-step size \[yr\]. Must be > 0. |
| `maximum_rel` | float | `1.0` | Time-fraction allowance added to ``dt.maximum`` on every step \[dimensionless\]. The effective per-step cap is the sum ``dt.maximum + maximum_rel * Time``, so at the default 1.0 the allowance grows linearly with simulation Time, and the absolute ``dt.maximum`` acts as the early-time floor (cap doubles at ``Time = dt.maximum``). Set ``maximum_rel = 0.0`` to disable the time-proportional allowance and recover the strict ``dt = min(dt.maximum, ...)`` cap. Must be >= 0. |
| `initial` | float | `30.0` | Initial time-step size \[yr\]. Must be > 0. |
| `mushy_maximum` | float | `0.0` | Maximum time-step size \[yr\] during the mushy-zone transition (``phi_crit < Phi_global < mushy_upper``). Tighter than ``maximum`` because the interior solver hits stiffness cliffs in this regime (phase-boundary Jgrav + rheology contrast). Set to 0 (default) to disable the mushy-regime cap, in which case ``maximum`` applies throughout. A typical value for Aragog at 1 M_E is ~4e3 yr; see ``input/tutorials/tutorial_earth.toml``. Must be >= 0. |
| `mushy_upper` | float | `0.99` | Upper bound of the mushy regime \[dimensionless melt fraction\]. When ``Phi_global < mushy_upper`` AND ``Phi_global > stop.solid.phi_crit``, ``mushy_maximum`` takes over from ``maximum``. Default 0.99 so the cap kicks in as soon as the first cell crystallises. Must be > 0 and < 1. |
| `evection_maximum` | float or none | `none` | Ceiling on the time-step size \[yr\] while the planet-satellite system is inside, or approaching, the evection resonance band. Must be > 0 when set. Default ``'none'`` (disables the whole mechanism). Must be > 0. |
| `evection_target_rel_de` | float | `0.05` | Target maximum fractional change in ``eccentricity_sat`` per macro-step while inside/approaching the evection band. Obliqua's own adaptive mode-window selection is keyed on the eccentricity it is given at call time, and that window is then held fixed for the whole of the following macro-step, so a large fractional swing in ``e`` within one step risks needing modes outside that window. Default 0.05 (5%). Must be > 0. |
| `evection_de_floor` | float | `0.02` | Floor on the eccentricity value used in the ``evection_target_rel_de`` ratio's denominator, so a tiny eccentricity right at capture onset does not make the allowed step blow up. Default 0.02. Must be > 0. |
| `evection_rate_window` | int | `2` | Number of trailing accepted macro-steps used to estimate the SECULAR ``|de/dt|`` this cap bounds against (a least-squares linear fit for windows > 2, the plain two-point difference at the default of 2). Default 2, preserves the two-point behaviour. Must be >= 2. |
| `evection_growth_factor` | float or none | `none` | Cap on the dt growth ratio between consecutive steps while the system is inside/approaching the evection band, or within ``evection_cooldown_iters`` steps of having left it. Separate from the global ``max_growth_factor`` (which most evection runs leave disabled, since it would also throttle ordinary bulk evolution for the rest of the run). Must be > 0 when set. Default ``'none'`` (disabled). Must be > 0. |
| `evection_cooldown_iters` | int or none | `none` | Number of PROTEUS iterations, after the system is no longer judged in/near the evection band, during which ``evection_growth_factor`` remains active. Refreshed to this value on every iteration the zone is active, so a long stay in the band does not exhaust it before exit. Must be > 0 when set. Default ``'none'`` (no cooldown tail; growth limiting turns off the instant the zone is left). Must be > 0. |
| `hysteresis_iters` | int | `0` | Number of PROTEUS iterations after an adaptive "slow down" decision during which the speed-up factor is suppressed. Prevents the controller from ramping dt straight back into the same stiffness cliff it just escaped from. Default 3; set to 0 to disable. Must be >= 0. |
| `hysteresis_sfinc` | float | `1.1` | Replacement speed-up factor applied while the hysteresis counter is active. Must be ``>= 1.0`` and ``<= SFINC`` (1.6). Default 1.1 (gentle ramp-up). Must be >= 1.0. |
| `impact_maximum` | float | `0.0` | Ceiling \[yr\] for the step that reaches a scheduled giant impact. Such a step is otherwise clamped only to the time left before the impact, which after a long quiescent phase can itself be large. With the ceiling set, a reaching step longer than ``max(impact_maximum, dtfloor)`` (dtfloor = dt.minimum + dt.minimum_rel * Time) is cut to an equal fraction of the time left; later steps are evaluated again, and the step that lands is no longer than ``max(impact_maximum, dtfloor)``. Set to 0 (default) to disable. Independent of this setting, the step that lands on an impact can be shorter than dtfloor, a step ending at most 1e-3 yr short of an impact is extended onto it (unless the step already reaches stop.time.maximum), and an impact is applied at the end of the first step that reaches its time. Impacts each less than 1e-3 yr after the one before form a chain that the step aims at the last of, so an impact in a chain can be applied later than its time by up to the chain span; a chain spanning 1e-3 yr or more is logged as a warning. Must be >= 0. |
| `max_growth_factor` | float | `0.0` | Cap on the dt growth ratio between consecutive steps \[dimensionless\]. Bounds dtswitch / dtprev, preventing large jumps that can wedge the interior solver; 0 (default) disables the cap. After a step that landed on a giant impact, dtprev is the larger of that step and ``min(dtfloor, last step that did not land on an impact)``, or dtfloor when there is no such step. Must be >= 0. |
<!-- END GENERATED: config-table [params.dt] -->

## Termination criteria `[params.stop]`

Each criterion can be independently enabled. The simulation terminates when any
enabled criterion is satisfied. Set `strict = true` to require the criterion
to be satisfied for two consecutive iterations before terminating.

## Run-row invariants `[invariants]`

At the end of each iteration, `check_row_invariants` evaluates coupled energy, structure, volatile-mass, and state-bounds invariants according to `invariants.mode` (`"off"`, `"report"`, or `"stop"`). All energy checks are report-only in every active mode (`report_only=True`, so status code 30 is reserved and never written by `mode = "stop"`). Note that `assert_mass_conservation` runs earlier in the main loop after `update_planet_mass` (`Proteus.start`) at a fixed $10^{-6}$ relative tolerance on `M_atm <= M_planet` and `M_vol_atm` versus the summed volatile gas species (and, when solid-phase volatile trapping is active, on per-element reservoir closure at `outgas.solver_rtol`), raising `RuntimeError` regardless of `invariants.mode`; with `outgas.vapourise = true`, rock vapour enters `M_atm` without leaving the interior, so the `M_atm <= M_planet` half of `assert_mass_conservation` logs a warning when the excess exceeds `M_vaps` while the volatile gas species sum check stays enforced. Helpfiles without `M_vol_atm` fail the `M_vol_atm_species_sum` check whenever any volatile gas species has non-zero atmospheric mass.

Each default tolerance is sized from the empirical residual distribution in post-closure runs (`fwl-aragog >= 26.10.1`): `energy_residual_rtol = 2.6e-4` sits above the $2.51\times 10^{-4}$ maximum gross-normalized cumulative energy residual across the 53 post-closure baseline corpus runs (coarser-step configurations such as `input/minimal.toml` at $2.367\times 10^{-3}$ and `minimal_quick` at $4.69\times 10^{-4}$ exceed this threshold and log under report mode); `step_energy_rtol = 1.0e-2` and `step_energy_smin_rtol = 5.0e-2` bound the per-step energy increment normalized by per-step gross flux when `T_magma > T(P_surf, S_min) + 0.5 K` (or when no P-S EOS table is present) and when `T_magma <= T(P_surf, S_min) + 0.5 K`, where $T(P_{\text{surf}}, S_{\min})$ is interpolated linearly in pressure at each row's `P_surf` on the $S_{\min}$ block of the run's cached P-S EOS table `temperature_solid.dat` (e.g. $302.342\text{ K}$ in `run_20261018_131253_ea68` and $323.208\text{ K}$ in `tutorial_earth` at $1\text{ bar}$ for $S_{\min} = 106.116\text{ J kg}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$ in the dynamic PALEOS-2phase $\text{MgSiO}_3$ tables, and $260.0\text{ K}$ at $P = 0$ for $S_{\min} = -84.786\text{ J kg}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$ in the Wolf & Bower 2018 1 TPa $\text{MgSiO}_3$ solid table; the raw P-T source `paleos_mgsio3_tables_pt_proteus_solid.dat` has $300.488\text{ K}$ at $P = 2.660\text{ GPa}$ rather than surface pressure, while the $0.5\text{ K}$ margin bounds the smooth low-pressure P-S linear interpolation error $\le 9.49\times 10^{-3}\text{ K}$ and static-mesh versus row `P_surf` drift $-0.0042\text{ K}$ to $+0.071\text{ K}$ across $S_{\min}$-clipped corpus rows, $< 0.5\text{ K}$ for $|P_{\text{mesh}} - P_{\text{surf}}| \le 1{,}748\text{ bar}$, well below the $+22.74\text{ K}$ to $+30.00\text{ K}$ first unclipped entropy-grid step; in post-closure default runs, the per-step increment has 99th percentile $5.4\times 10^{-4}$, 99.9th percentile $2.7\times 10^{-2}$, and maximum $0.117$ outside the $S_{\min}$ temperature clip, and a maximum of $4.39\%$ on the clip); `solver_residual_rtol = 1.0e-12` bounds the ODE solver residual normalized by gross throughput above the $2.46\times 10^{-14}$ converged maximum; `struct_mass_desync_warn_rtol = 5.0e-3` and `struct_mass_desync_rtol = 1.0e-2` sit above the $4.71\times 10^{-3}$ post-closure structure mass desync maximum; `interior_mass_target_rtol = 3.0e-3` sits above the $2.05\times 10^{-3}$ Zalmoxis interior mass update maximum; `core_mass_target_rtol = 2.5e-2` sits at about $1.6$ times the $1.565\times 10^{-2}$ maximum radial-trapezoidal core mass difference on the default $1\,M_{\oplus}$ Zalmoxis structure run `a627_default` (99th percentile $1.518\times 10^{-2}$, which lies outside the 68 finished post-closure default runs; $1.004\times 10^{-2}$ maximum and $9.79\times 10^{-3}$ 99th percentile across those 68 runs); and `element_closure_rtol = 2.5e-4` sits at $2.5$ times the default `outgas.solver_rtol = 1.0e-4`.

The cumulative energy fractions (`E_residual_cons_frac_gross`, `solver_residual_frac`, and `E_core_residual_frac`) are evaluated on finite values only once prior post-init rows in `hf_all` have non-zero gross flux throughput (`hist_gross > 0`, which in a coupled run holds from row 5 onward after the initialization stage and first post-init step, clearing all 22 early core-residual transients, 543 early energy-residual rows, and 3 early solver-residual rows in the corpus while still flagging non-finite values on every row). Cumulative and carried-forward checks (`E_residual_cons_frac_gross`, `escape_cumulative_bound`, `struct_mass_desync_frac`, `M_core_target_rel_err`, and `M_int_target_rel_err`) suppress repeated warnings at the same `(name, report_only)` level in report mode, and for report-only violations in stop mode (re-logging when a carried-forward structure column changes value on a new structure solve, when a suppressed check transitions to a non-finite value or between `NaN` and signed infinities, or when a check escalates from warning to stop level), and accumulate total row counts in the end-of-run summary.

When `outgas.module = 'calliope'`, the per-element reservoir closure check in `check_volatile_invariants` uses `outgas.mass_thresh + element_closure_rtol * max(total, 0)` (including when `total <= 0`, so a zero-budget leak is seen above `mass_thresh`), whereas when `outgas.module != 'calliope'` it uses `max(element_closure_atol_kg, element_closure_rtol * max(total, 0))` (independently, when solid-phase volatile trapping is active, `coupler.assert_mass_conservation` checks element closure at `outgas.solver_rtol` earlier in the loop). Because `outgas.mass_thresh` defaults to $10^{16}\text{ kg}$ while CALLIOPE's internal noble-gas solver uses $\max(\text{rtol} \times \text{target}, 10\text{ kg})$ with $\text{rtol} = 10^{-4}$ (`solve.py` at tag `26.10.05`), the ratio $(10^{16} + 2.5\times 10^{-4}\,\text{total}) / \max(10^{-4}\,\text{total}, 10\text{ kg})$ makes the `calliope` closure check $2.5\times 10^{4}\text{ to }10^{7}$ times looser than CALLIOPE's internal noble-gas gate on typical $10^{13}\text{ to }4\times 10^{15}\text{ kg}$ noble-gas inventories (and $2.8\text{ to }11.2$ times looser on the $1.15\times 10^{19}\text{ to }2.88\times 10^{20}\text{ kg}$ noble-gas inventories in the corpus), so it does not catch noble-gas non-closure below `outgas.mass_thresh`. When `planet.fO2_source = 'from_O_budget'`, `escape_cumulative_bound` is `report_only=True` because sub-threshold element flooring in `calc_new_elements` zeroes an element total below `outgas.mass_thresh` without crediting `esc_kg_cumulative` or `M_desiccated`.

When `outgas.vapourise = false`, `outgas/wrapper.py` resets the atmospheric and total inventories of the rock-forming vapour elements (`vap_element_list`: `Si`, `Mg`, `Fe`, `Na`, `Al`, `Ti`, `Ca`, `K`, `V`) to zero on each step, so `check_volatile_invariants` enforces reservoir closure across all elements in `element_list` except derived oxygen under `planet.fO2_source = 'user_constant'`. When `outgas.vapourise = true`, `check_volatile_invariants` skips element reservoir closure for the rock-forming vapour elements (`vap_element_list`, whose totals remain zero while rock vapour enters the atmosphere) and for all volatile and noble-gas elements that `lavatmos` overwrites from gas-phase equilibrium without updating the element totals (`LAVATMOS_OVERWRITTEN_ELEMENTS`: `H`, `C`, `N`, `S`, `O`, and `noble_gases` `He`, `Ne`, `Ar`, `Kr`, `Xe`), while keeping the non-negative reservoir bounds checks (`{e}_kg_{r}_bounds`) and non-finite mass checks active for every element in `element_list`.

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED: config-table [invariants] -->
<!-- Generated by tools/generate_config_reference.py; edit src/proteus/config/, not this table -->
| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | str | `"report"` | Enforcement mode for run-row invariants: ``'off'``, ``'report'``, or ``'stop'``. Energy checks are report-only in every active mode (status code 30 is reserved). Choices: `"off"`, `"report"`, `"stop"`. |
| `energy_residual_rtol` | float | `0.00026` | Relative tolerance on cumulative coupled energy residual against gross throughput \[-\], evaluated once prior post-init rows have non-zero gross throughput (report-only). Sized above the ``2.51e-4`` maximum gross-normalized residual across the 53 post-closure baseline corpus runs (coarser-step configs ``input/minimal.toml`` and ``minimal_quick`` reach ``2.37e-3`` and ``4.69e-4``). | `step_energy_rtol` | float | `0.01` | Relative tolerance on per-step energy residual increment normalized by per-step gross flux when ``T_magma > T(P_surf, S_min) + 0.5 K`` (or for all rows when no P-S EOS table is present) \[-\] (report-only). ## Constraints

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED: config-constraints params -->
<!-- Generated by tools/generate_config_reference.py; edit src/proteus/config/, not this table -->
Cross-field constraints enforced when the config file loads:

- Reject accretion runs with a stratified Aragog core_module core.
- Reject accretion runs on an interior that cannot apply an impact.
- Reject accretion runs that also vapourise rock into the atmosphere.
- Reject an Aragog core_module core that its structure or solver cannot serve.
- Check that required external packages are importable for the selected modules.
- Require structure mass desync stop tolerance to be at least the warning tolerance.
- The maximum must exceed the minimum on the same section.
- Reject giant impacts with the parameterized star-planet model.
- Require S_min step energy tolerance to be at least step_energy_rtol.
